summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of Crohn’s disease, status post subtotal colectomy, was readmitted five days after discharge due to recurrent right lower quadrant abdominal pain and 22 episodes of non-bloody, watery, black stools in 24 hours. He also reported ongoing sweats, cough with dark sputum, and mild nausea. He was treated for an acute flare of Crohn’s disease with IV fluids, IV methylprednisolone, and restart of azathioprine. Pain was managed with IV medications, and he was transitioned to oral prednisone with a slow taper. He improved clinically, resumed a regular diet, and had resolution of sweats. Stool studies showed no infectious cause. Vitamin D deficiency was addressed with supplementation. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to follow up with his GI physician, complete outpatient lab work, and avoid opioids. Smoking cessation was strongly encouraged.
